specification.problem: Show that quantum circuit depth in the adaptive nearest-neighbor architecture, where a classical controller chooses which local interactions to apply on the kD grid Z^k with k>=2, matches (up to a constant factor) the depth in the standard model with arbitrary pairwise interactions. Also give optimal non-adaptive circuits for controlled operations and fanout on a kD grid.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level problem statement and depth/size/width scaling relations only. No explicit circuit construction, simulation protocol, or measurement scheme is reconstructed from the abstract.

specification.initial_state: Assumed: control in arbitrary state, targets in arbitrary state; any ancillas (within Θ(n) width) start in |0>.

steps.description: Embed the control and n targets in a kD grid of side Θ(n^{1/k}), using Θ(n) total qubits including ancillas.
Assumed: spread the control value across the grid by nearest-neighbor copying (CNOT) steps, covering distance Θ(n^{1/k}).
Apply the local controlled operations on each target using the copies, then uncompute the copies by reversing the spreading, giving non-adaptive depth Θ(n^{1/k}) and size Θ(n).
For the adaptive result: a standard-model circuit is simulated on the grid with classical control, at constant-factor depth overhead. The mechanism is not given in the abstract.

specification.measurement: The abstract specifies no measurement for the controlled-operation/fanout circuits. Assumed: computational-basis measurement of the output qubits, or of the Shor period-register qubits when simulating Shor's algorithm. In the adaptive model, mid-circuit measurement outcomes may be used by the classical controller to choose later local interactions; the details are not given.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Not specified in the abstract. For Shor's algorithm, the standard continued-fractions and gcd postprocessing would apply (background assumption). The classical controller computes the interaction schedule.
